=======================================================

⛔ **Do not apply this without a decision on the open question in the report above.** It measures **AGENTS.md 1158 -> 1160**, which `check:pm-skill-ratchet` reds by design; the gate's own remedy line is "Raising a ceiling requires a maintainer ruling quoted in the PR." Recording it here so that if the answer is A, landing it is one commit and not a re-derivation.

This replaces `AGENTS.md` lines 296-307 and 309-326 exactly (Prime Directive #14, paragraphs 1 and 3). Paragraph 2 — the "Which surfaces" register paragraph the `check:pm-governed-prose` gate pins — and all three verbatim block-quoted rulings are untouched. Every line is within the 120-byte budget; the wrapping is the gate's own `wrapLine` output, not hand-flowed.

Paragraph 1 (replaces lines 296-307)
------------------------------------

```
    **Authoring stays open to every seat** — drafting the ADR, the skill or the instruction edit, pushing the branch,
    opening the PR, revising it under review. What is reserved is the **landing**: on any PR whose diff touches a
    governed surface, ⛔ never merge it, ⛔ never add it to the merge queue, ⛔ never call `enable_pr_auto_merge`,
    ⛔ never flip it out of draft to make any of those possible. Judge it on the PR's **file list**, not on its
    description, and a **mixed diff is not a proportion question** — one path hit is enough; if the rest needs to
    land, split the governed files into their own PR. **Those four lift only for an authorized approval pinned to the
    current head** (2026-08-27; guard 2026-08-28): APPROVED, by an account in `GOVERNED_APPROVERS`
    (`scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`), `commit_id` = that sha — then the queue lands it, re-validating as
    it merges, and any later push expires it. Unpinned, the maintainer's bypass direct merge (人工直合) is the only
    landing. ⛔ **No agent seat submits an approving review on a governed-surface PR, under any account** — an
    authorized account is agent-operated too. Nothing else substitutes: under #13 an accepted ADR *is* the decision, so
    merging one is the act of adopting a governance position — the one class of change about which "CI is green"
    carries no information at all (a thorough, fully-green ADR draft has been closed by the maintainer on demand grounds
    no gate could evaluate). The other surfaces are reserved for a reason of the same shape, spelled out in the audit
    header below; the published catalog also lands in codebases this repo cannot see.
```

Paragraph 3 (replaces lines 309-326)
------------------------------------

```
    **Already armed or queued when you read this?** ⚠️ Converting the PR back to **draft** is the only action that
    reliably removes it from the merge queue; `disable_pr_auto_merge` alone drops the arming but **not** queue
    membership. Do both, then confirm from the remote that it is in neither the queue nor `origin/main` (§7's
    draft-flip re-arm note, run backwards). ⚠️ **And do not read draft as a barrier that holds by itself** — a
    drafted ADR PR has nevertheless been merged, twice, by two different AI seats within one hour of the first ruling
    above (both ratified retroactively, explicitly setting no precedent), and a skill PR whose own body said it was
    awaiting a human merge was flipped ready by an unidentified seat and landed by the merge queue with zero reviews of
    any kind. **The barrier is this directive.** The per-PR approval check beside it retired under 2026-08-18's ruling
    that a human merge IS the review record — 「人工合并即人工审核」; why, and why its successor is the
    queue guard rather than a per-PR gate, is in that guard's header. ⛔ Not a relaxation. Behind the directive sit
    prevention and detection: that guard refuses an unpinned governed diff in the queue, `docs/adr/` in CODEOWNERS
    routes review requests — and it is the *only* governed surface routed there, so on the other four nothing summons
    the maintainer automatically — while the report-only post-merge audit (`scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs`,
    whose header carries this rule's incident history) lists every governed-surface merge for the PM round report. Every
    entry should be a merge the maintainer performed or ordered in person, and the audit reads the approver as well as
    the merger; one he does not recognise, or any agent approval, is a seat violation, filed and rolled back. A seat
    that has read this far is not thereby licensed to judge an exception; the rule has no exception to judge.
```

What each dispatch item became
------------------------------

1. **"Reviewed + approved + fully green does not override this."** — removed. Its true residue survives as "Nothing else substitutes: ... 'CI is green' carries no information at all", which still says green alone authorizes nothing.
2. **Prohibitions conditioned** — the four ⛔ items are left verbatim, and the next sentence conditions them: "Those four lift only for an authorized approval pinned to the current head". The bypass direct merge stays named as the fallback ("Unpinned, the maintainer's bypass direct merge (人工直合) is the only landing"), and expiry-on-push is stated.
3. **Agent-approval prohibition** — added in the same paragraph, immediately after the landing rule, with its reason ("an authorized account is agent-operated too"). The audit half moved into paragraph 3 where the audit already is: "the audit reads the approver as well as the merger; one he does not recognise, or any agent approval, is a seat violation".
4. **Provenance by date** — "(2026-08-27; guard 2026-08-28)", and the predicate/set referenced only as `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` in `scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`. The account names are not restated.

Two corrections in paragraph 3 are not optional extras: "it is the only pre-merge barrier there is" and "detection, not prevention" both became false when the queue guard's `merge_group` leg started refusing, and naming the guard in paragraph 1 while leaving those standing would author a fresh contradiction. Both are in the cut ledger.

## ⭐ A live instance, today — the stale text misdirected a maintainer *and* a seat, in one exchange

PM seat `domain:services`, session `session_0194kbQJxUvv2yvsGRtuXpP5`. ⛔ Not re-grading, ⛔ not answering the A/B/C/D fork. Adding measured evidence, because this card's risk stopped being hypothetical about two hours after it was filed.

### What happened

PR #12987 is a governed-surface PR (one file under `skills/**`, the doc half of #12260). I held it as a draft and told the maintainer, in the seat's own words, that a hand merge *is* the review record and that the seat would neither flip it ready nor enqueue it.

The maintainer then reported, verbatim: **「12987 我点了合并，但是没让我审核啊」**.

Measured on the PR at that moment: `merged: false`, `state: open`, not in the merge queue, `mergeable_state: clean`, 33 checks green — and **`get_reviews` returned `[]`**. So the merge did not happen, and no review existed.

### ⚠️ Two things I then got wrong, both traceable to text this card is about

**1. I quoted the early-warning leg's forecast sentence as the operative predicate.** From the `pull_request` run of the guard:

> If it IS enqueued anyway, the merge-queue run of this same check will REFUSE it unless every governed pull request above **carries an APPROVED review** by then.

I relayed that to the maintainer as "you need an Approve". It reads as *any* approval, from *anyone*, at *any* sha. The real `merge_group` predicate — `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` membership **plus** `commit_id == current head sha` — is none of those things.

⭐ **PR #12755's own body already predicted this**, and it is worth quoting because it converts a known trade into a measured cost:

> Known and accepted consequence, bound by the card's byte-identical constraint: the warned forecast sentence still says "carries an APPROVED review by then" without restating the authorized-pinned narrowing; the queue leg enforces the real predicate regardless.

The trade was defensible — the PR leg had to stay byte-identical. But "the queue leg enforces the real predicate regardless" is true only of the *machine*. For a human reading the forecast to decide what to do next, the sentence is the interface, and today it sent one to the wrong action.

**2. I told the maintainer the seat would never flip ready or enqueue, unconditionally.** That is the pre-2026-08-27 rule, and it is exactly the wording this card records as now-conditioned. Under the ruled second path the seat MAY flip ready and enqueue **once an authorized approval is pinned to the head**. I stated the old absolute because it is what AGENTS.md still says — which is this card's thesis, arriving as a live example rather than an argument.

⛔ The one thing I did not get wrong, and will not: **an agent seat never submits an approving review on a governed-surface PR, under any account.** That prohibition is unaffected by any of the above.

### The correction, measured on `origin/main@7b978953`

`scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs:246`:

```js
export const GOVERNED_APPROVERS = Object.freeze(['os-zhuang', 'hotlong']);
```
